advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Consider deriving the probe's `lean_dropped` set from `rebar._engine_support.reads.LEAN_OMITTED_FIELDS` (or leave a comment justifying the intentional independent restatement) so the drop set has one source of truth.
evidence: src/rebar/_engine_support/reads.py:412 `LEAN_OMITTED_FIELDS: tuple[str, ...] = (...)` is the single source of truth the unit test (tests/unit/test_pinned_ticket_view.py) imports, but the probe copies the values instead
ABSENCE: the probe does not `from rebar._engine_support.reads import LEAN_OMITTED_FIELDS`, unlike the unit test which does
advisory.finding: The golden-path probe re-declares the lean drop set as a local literal `lean_dropped = {...}` instead of importing `LEAN_OMITTED_FIELDS`, so a future change to the shared constant will not be tracked by the probe's derived expectation and the two spellings can silently diverge.
scenarios: A later ticket adds/removes a field from LEAN_OMITTED_FIELDS but forgets to update the probe's local set: the probe's drift assertion no longer matches the real contract.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Extend a CLI list test to assert the four signature fields (authorship_ledger/attestations/signature/keyring) are absent from a lean `rebar list --output json` row and present under `--full`.
evidence: test_list_lean_by_default_omits_body asserts only bodies: `assert "description" not in lean` / `assert "comments" not in lean` (tests/interfaces/store/test_reducer_single_source.py:142-143) with no assertion on authorship_ledger/attestations/signature/keyring
release-notes.md diff: 'CLI `rebar list --output json` narrows because it shares the same projection — its row goes from 39 keys to 35, losing exactly those four'

Added lines src/rebar/_engine_support/reads.py:525-526 route include_body=False CLI list through lean_projection, so the CLI narrowing is newly introduced by lines in this diff; a `rebar list --output json` row for a ticket carrying signature material is the named input whose four fields the added lines now drop
advisory.finding: The CLI `rebar list --output json` lean-row narrowing — a user-visible breaking change dropping exactly authorship_ledger/attestations/signature/keyring (39->35 keys per the release notes) — has no updated unit/integration test asserting those four fields leave the CLI JSON row. The existing CLI test test_list_lean_by_default_omits_body still asserts only description/comments; the four new drops on the CLI surface are exercised only by the golden-path probe, which requires a real store carrying signature material.
scenarios: A regression that re-adds a signature field to the CLI lean JSON row (e.g. the CLI path bypassing lean_projection) would pass every added unit test and only be caught by the real-store probe

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Seed the pinned-view parity test with a ticket carrying signature material (or reuse a bulky state) so the LEAN_OMITTED_FIELDS drop assertion is non-trivial on both backends.
evidence: Fixtures create tickets with only a description and a comment: `rebar.create_ticket(... description="a body" ...)` / `rebar.comment(child, "a comment", ...)` (tests/unit/test_pinned_ticket_view.py:863-866) — no signing occurs, so authorship_ledger/attestations/signature/keyring are absent from public_state before projection
Assertion loop: `for field in LEAN_OMITTED_FIELDS: assert field not in snapshot_rows[0]` (tests/unit/test_pinned_ticket_view.py:881-883)
advisory.finding: In test_snapshot_backend_lean_projection_matches_the_event_log_backend the `for field in LEAN_OMITTED_FIELDS: assert field not in row` loop passes trivially for the four signature fields (authorship_ledger/attestations/signature/keyring): the freshly created parent/child tickets carry no signature material, so those keys were never present in either row and the assertion cannot distinguish 'projection dropped them' from 'they never existed'. Only description/comments are meaningfully exercised by this test's drop assertion.
scenarios: A regression where lean_projection stops dropping signature fields would not be caught by THIS test (they are absent regardless); it is caught instead only by the MCP bulky_store tests

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Decide whether CLI `rebar ready` should mirror MCP `ready_tickets`' lean-by-default narrowing (add a `--full` flag and lean projection) or explicitly document why CLI `ready` stays full.
evidence: diff src/rebar/_mcp_reads.py: `def ready_tickets(sort: str | None = None, full: bool = False) -> list[TicketStateOut]:` now lean-by-default via `_discovery_rows(rebar.ready(sort=sort), full=full)`
src/rebar/_engine_support/reads.py:553: `states = [public_state(s) for s in find_ready_tickets(...)]` — ready_states returns full state, no projection
docs/release-notes.md:29-35: narrowing table lists CLI `rebar list`, MCP `list_tickets`, MCP `ready_tickets` but never CLI `rebar ready` — divergence unjustified
advisory.finding: MCP `ready_tickets` was narrowed to a lean-by-default row with a new `full=False` opt-out (src/rebar/_mcp_reads.py:371 via `_discovery_rows`/`lean_projection`), but the sibling CLI adapter `rebar ready` (`_cmd_ready`) was not updated: it still emits the FULL ticket shape (calls `ready_states` -> full `public_state`, dumps verbatim) and gained no `--full` flag, so the same 'ready to work' discovery operation now returns different default shapes on the MCP and CLI surfaces.
scenarios: An agent calls MCP `ready_tickets` and a human runs `rebar ready --output json` expecting the same shape; the CLI still carries authorship_ledger/attestations/signature/keyring while MCP drops them.

A consumer migrating off the signature-bulk fields is told (release notes) to pass `--full` on the CLI, but `rebar ready` has no `--full` and is already full — the migration guidance does not apply consistently.
advisory.suggested_fix: Mirror the MCP narrowing onto the CLI: add a `--full` flag to `build_ready` and, in `_cmd_ready`, project the rows lean unless `--full` (e.g. `states = states if ns.full else [lean_projection(s) for s in states]`) using `rebar._engine_support.reads.lean_projection`, so `rebar ready` and MCP `ready_tickets` share one default shape.
